points.title: 乡村童年
points.description: 1881年8月6日，亚历山大·弗莱明出生于苏格兰艾尔郡洛赫菲尔德的一个农场家庭。他是八个孩子中的第七个。父亲休·弗莱明是农场主，母亲格蕾丝是当地教师的女儿。这段乡村生活培养了他对自然和科学的浓厚兴趣，尤其是观察和实验的能力。弗莱明在乡村学校接受基础教育，展现出对自然界的敏锐观察力，这种能力后来成为他科学发现的重要基础。
points.descriptionEn: Born on August 6, 1881, at Lochfield Farm in Ayrshire, Scotland, Alexander Fleming was the seventh of eight children in a farming family. His father, Hugh Fleming, was a farmer, and his mother, Grace, was the daughter of a local schoolmaster. This rural upbringing fostered his deep interest in nature and science, particularly his skills in observation and experimentation. Fleming received his basic education at local schools, demonstrating keen observational abilities of the natural world that would later become fundamental to his scientific discoveries.

points.title: 医学启蒙
points.description: 1901年，弗莱明进入伦敦圣玛丽医学院学习医学。在这里，他遇到了对他一生影响深远的导师阿尔姆罗兹·赖特爵士，这位免疫学先驱开创了疫苗研究的新领域。弗莱明在医学院期间表现出色，获得了多项奖学金和奖项。1906年，他完成医学学业后留在圣玛丽医院担任赖特的助手，开始专注于细菌学研究。这段经历为他后来的抗生素发现奠定了坚实的科学基础。
points.descriptionEn: In 1901, Fleming entered St. Mary's Medical School in London to study medicine. There he met Sir Almroth Wright, a pioneer in immunology whose work would profoundly influence his career. Fleming excelled in his studies, earning several scholarships and awards. After completing his medical education in 1906, he remained at St. Mary's Hospital as Wright's assistant, beginning his focus on bacteriology research. This period laid the scientific foundation for his later discovery of antibiotics.

points.title: 战地医生
points.description: 第一次世界大战爆发后，弗莱明作为皇家陆军医疗队的成员被派往法国索姆河前线。这段经历让他亲眼目睹了伤口感染的致命后果，当时缺乏有效的抗生素治疗。他注意到许多士兵因简单的伤口感染而死亡，这促使他思考如何预防感染。弗莱明开发了一种名为'赖特-弗莱明方法'的防腐剂，用于处理伤口，虽然效果有限，但显示了他对解决感染问题的执着。这段战地经历深刻影响了他后来的研究方向，成为他发现青霉素的动机之一。
points.descriptionEn: After the outbreak of World War I in 1914, Fleming was sent to the Somme Front in France as a member of the Royal Army Medical Corps. This experience exposed him firsthand to the fatal consequences of wound infections, for which there were no effective treatments at the time. He observed how many soldiers died from simple wound infections, which prompted him to consider infection prevention. Fleming developed the 'Wright-Fleming method' of antiseptic treatment for wounds, which had limited effectiveness but demonstrated his persistence in solving infection problems. This wartime experience profoundly influenced his later research direction and became a key motivation for his discovery of penicillin.

points.title: 青霉素发现
points.description: 1928年9月，弗莱明在圣玛丽医院的研究室进行葡萄球菌研究时，意外发现一个被霉菌污染的培养皿中，葡萄球菌被杀死。经过仔细研究，他确认这种霉菌（后来被鉴定为青霉菌）能够产生一种物质杀死细菌。1929年，他发表了关于青霉素的论文，但当时未能提纯这种物质，因此其应用受到限制。弗莱明继续研究青霉素，但直到1940年，牛津大学的霍华德·弗洛里和恩斯特·钱恩才成功提纯并证明了青霉素的临床价值。这一发现彻底改变了医学史，开启了抗生素时代。
points.descriptionEn: In September 1928, while studying Staphylococcus at St. Mary's Hospital, Fleming made a serendipitous discovery when he noticed that a mold-contaminated petri dish had killed the bacteria. Upon careful examination, he confirmed that this mold (later identified as Penicillium notatum) produced a substance that killed bacteria. In 1929, he published his paper on penicillin, but was unable to purify the substance at the time, limiting its application. Fleming continued his research on penicillin, but it wasn't until 1940 that Howard Florey and Ernst Chain at Oxford University successfully purified and demonstrated its clinical value. This discovery revolutionized medical history and ushered in the age of antibiotics.

points.title: 晚年荣誉
points.description: 1945年，弗莱明与霍华德·弗洛里和恩斯特·钱恩共同获得诺贝尔生理学或医学奖，以表彰他们对青霉素的发现及其在治疗传染病方面的应用。战后，弗莱明成为国际知名的科学家，担任多个医学组织的荣誉职位。他继续研究细菌学，并致力于医学教育。1951年，他被任命为爱丁堡大学校长。1955年3月11日，弗莱明在伦敦去世，享年73岁。他的发现拯救了数百万人的生命，被誉为'20世纪最伟大的医学发现之一'，他的名字成为医学进步的象征。
points.descriptionEn: In 1945, Fleming shared the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine with Howard Florey and Ernst Chain for the discovery of penicillin and its therapeutic applications in treating infectious diseases. After the war, Fleming became internationally renowned as a scientist, holding honorary positions in various medical organizations. He continued his research in bacteriology and dedicated himself to medical education. In 1951, he was appointed Rector of the University of Edinburgh. On March 11, 1955, Fleming died in London at the age of 73. His discovery has saved millions of lives and is regarded as 'one of the greatest medical discoveries of the 20th century,' with his name becoming a symbol of medical progress.

supporter.zh: 亚历山大·弗莱明被视为现代医学的英雄，他的偶然发现开创了抗生素时代，拯救了数百万人的生命。支持者赞扬他敏锐的观察力和对科学的执着，将他的发现视为医学史上最重要的突破之一。弗莱明代表了科学发现中偶然性与准备性相结合的典范，他的谦逊态度和对科学纯粹性的追求也备受推崇。他的遗产不仅在于青霉素本身，更在于他启发了无数科学家继续探索未知领域。
supporter.en: Alexander Fleming is regarded as a hero of modern medicine whose serendipitous discovery开创了 the age of antibiotics, saving millions of lives. Supporters praise his keen observational skills and persistence in science, considering his discovery one of the most significant breakthroughs in medical history. Fleming represents the perfect combination of chance and preparation in scientific discovery, and his humility and dedication to scientific purity are highly esteemed. His legacy extends beyond penicillin itself to inspiring countless scientists to continue exploring unknown territories.

critic.zh: 批评者指出弗莱明的发现存在局限性，他未能将青霉素发展为可用药物，直到弗洛里和钱恩的工作才使其临床应用成为可能。有人认为他过度强调了偶然性，而低估了系统研究的重要性。此外，弗莱明晚年对细菌耐药性的警告被忽视，导致抗生素滥用问题日益严重。批评者还指出，诺贝尔奖的分配存在争议，因为弗莱明的主要贡献是初步发现，而非药物开发和临床应用。
critic.en: Critics point out limitations in Fleming's discovery, noting that he failed to develop penicillin into a usable drug, which was only achieved through the work of Florey and Chain. Some argue he overemphasized serendipity while underestimating the importance of systematic research. Additionally, Fleming's late-life warnings about antibiotic resistance were ignored, contributing to the growing problem of antibiotic misuse. Critics also note controversy in the Nobel Prize distribution, as Fleming's primary contribution was the initial discovery rather than drug development and clinical application.

objective.zh: 在历史学界和流行文化中，弗莱明被定义为科学偶然性的象征，同时也代表了科学进步的集体努力。他的故事常被简化为'偶然发现'的典范，但历史学家强调他的长期研究背景和科学素养是这一发现的基础。流行文化中，弗莱明常被描绘为孤独的天才，但现代历史研究更强调他与弗洛里、钱恩等科学家的合作。他的发现被视为20世纪医学革命的起点，同时也引发了关于科学发现中个人贡献与集体努力的持续讨论。
objective.en: In historical and popular culture, Fleming is defined as a symbol of scientific serendipity while also representing the collective effort behind scientific progress. His story is often simplified as a paradigm of 'accidental discovery,' but historians emphasize that his long-term research background and scientific literacy were fundamental to this finding. In popular culture, Fleming is frequently portrayed as a lone genius, but modern historical research emphasizes his collaboration with scientists like Florey and Chain. His discovery is seen as the starting point of the 20th-century medical revolution, while also sparking ongoing discussions about individual versus collective contributions in scientific discovery.

self.zh: 当我发现青霉素时，我并没有试图去发现什么，我只是做了我应该做的事情。
self.en: When I discovered penicillin, I didn't try to discover anything, I just did what I had to do.

others.zh: 弗莱明的发现是医学史上最伟大的事件之一，它使人类的平均寿命增加了约十年。
others.en: Fleming's discovery is one of the greatest events in medical history; it has added about ten years to the average human life span.
